chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that al-Hasan ibn Mayl al-Daqqaq narrated that Salma ibn al-Khattab narrated from Muni' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus, from Sabah al-Mazni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ascended [to Heaven] one hundred and twenty times. Every time, the Honorable, the Exalted God recommended to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) the Wilayah of Ali and the Imams (peace be upon them) more than He recommended the obligatory duties.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: Recommended/Instructed (God's act of emphasizing a command or right)
key_terms.الْفَرَائِض: Al-Fara'id (the obligatory ritual duties, such as prayer and fasting)
key_terms.عَرَجَ: Ascended (specifically referring to the Prophet's night journey or ascensions to Heaven)

ai.seo_question: How many times did the Prophet ascend to Heaven according to this hadith, and what was emphasized each time?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal*, this narration highlights the centrality of Imamate in Shia theology by comparing the frequency of divine emphasis on Wilayah against that of Fara'id (obligatory rituals) during the Prophet's ascensions. The report, transmitted through a chain including Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, underscores that spiritual authority and lineage were considered more critical to the faith's preservation than ritual law alone. This reinforces the Shia view that the Imams are the living embodiment of divine guidance, essential for interpreting the Sharia.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 26-5 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Al-Hassan ibn Matil al-Daq’qaq quoted Salma ibn al-Khat’tab, on the authority of Muni’a ibn al-Haj’jaj, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Sabah al-Mazny that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

The Prophet (MGB) ascended to Heaven one-hundred and twenty times. Every time, the Honorable the Exalted God recommended the love for Ali (MGB) and the Immaculate Divine Leaders (MGB) more than He recommended the obligatory deeds.”
